2.  Emergency Preparedness Month. Each September, National Preparedness Month is
  recognized to promote disaster and emergency planning, emphasizing the need to strengthen
  community resilience. This observance serves as a crucial reminder for residents to stay
  informed and be better equipped to handle emergencies.

  Police Department Retirees. Two recent retirees will be honored, Sergeant Martin Weinreb
  retired on May 2, 2024, after over 29 years of dedicated service to the City of La Verne, and

  2024, after a distinguished career spanning over 35 years.

 ADJOURNMENT T - IN MEMORY OF ERNIE SILVA

 Ernie, who was one of La Verne CERT'
  s long- term members, recently passed away. Ernie was a
 very warm, caring, passionate and dedicated team member who was always willing to assist in
 outreach, events, and trainings. Ernie moved to La Verne in 1999 where he had been heavily
 involved in his local community. Being an Eagle Scout himself, he enjoyed participating in Eagle
 Scout Boards of Review. He served on the Damien High School Consultative Board and was a
 member  and leader of the Shield Men'
  s Ministry for Holy Name of Mary Parish. Ernie was a
 hospitality minister, Eucharistic minister, and lector. He also was a member of the Knights of
 Columbus and served as a Council and Assembly officer. Ernie graduated LV CERT basic training in
 2017 and was a member since that time. Ernie  spent his entire career in the aerospace and special
 mission aircraft industry, leaving an impressive legacy complete with highly decorated accolades.
 Ernie is survived by his wife Elenor, his son Robert, and his lemon beagle, Argos. His presence will
 be greatly missed.
